description.value: Mount Robson Lodge is a family-owned cabin resort established in 1978, set 5 km west of the Mount Robson Provincial Park entrance on Yellowhead Highway 16, with direct views of BC's highest peak and a short walk to the Fraser River. Self-contained rustic cabins each sleep up to four guests and include a kitchenette, making the property a practical base for multi-day touring along the Yellowhead corridor. The lodge also operates Mount Robson Whitewater Rafting, so cyclists seeking an adventure rest day have options directly on site.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website loaded successfully and provides rich detail across multiple subpages. No mention of bike storage, bike-handling procedures, laundry, or most cycling-specific amenities appears anywhere on the site. The phone number displayed sitewide (111-011-1111) is not a valid Canadian number and is clearly a placeholder, making phone contact confirmation impossible.
concerns: Phone number listed sitewide (111-011-1111) is not a valid Canadian phone number and appears to be a placeholder; no usable phone contact available.
Website address is inconsistent: header and about-us page show 'Valemount, BC V0E 2Z0' while the footer uses 'Mt. Robson, BC V0E 2Z0'; postal code matches but the locality label differs.
OSM community field assigns this record to 'Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior', but the property is in the Robson Valley near Valemount, which falls in a different tourism region.
Cabins page notes there is no cell service at the property — relevant context for cyclists relying on mobile navigation.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The lodge is a legitimate and well-established accommodation on a key cycling corridor adjacent to Mount Robson Provincial Park, but neither secure bike storage nor staff bike procedures are mentioned anywhere on the website; direct contact is needed to confirm the WWC required criteria before inclusion.
enrichment_extras.notes: Three-night minimum stay policy noted on front page. Cabins include electricity, heat, running water, bathroom with shower/bath, and kitchenette — useful context for cyclists evaluating self-catering options.

Nearby evening food.detail: FAQ and cabins pages state Valemount (20-minute drive) and Jasper (1-hour drive) offer several dining options

Nearby grocery.detail: FAQ and cabins pages confirm closest grocery stores are in Valemount (20-minute drive) or Jasper (1-hour drive)
